column1: # Manuscript -> Overleaf project registry, consumed by scripts/overleaf_sync.sh
# One TAB-separated line per manuscript:
#   <dir name under OVERLEAF_DOCS_DIR>
# The project id is the last path segment of the Overleaf project URL:
#   https://www.overleaf.com/project/<PROJECT-ID>
#   git clone https://git@git.overleaf.com/<PROJECT-ID>
# The optional 3rd column is the subdirectory that maps to the Overleaf project
# ROOT. Omit it (or use ".") when the manuscript dir itself is the project root.
# Project ids are not credentials - they are useless without an authenticated
# Overleaf account - so this file is safe to track. Auth comes from the git
# credential helper configured for git.overleaf.com; NEVER put a token here.
# BayesBreak layout note
# paper/main.tex and book/main.tex both compile from docs/manuscripts/ as the
# working directory: they reference shared/ and paper/ as sibling paths.
# Therefore OVERLEAF_DOCS_DIR must be set to "docs" so that "manuscripts" maps
# to docs/manuscripts/ — the correct Overleaf project root.
#   export OVERLEAF_DOCS_DIR=docs
# If you use separate Overleaf projects for paper and book, each needs its own
# entry and its own copy of shared/ inside the project (Overleaf cannot resolve
# cross-project \input paths). Simplest: one project, set main document to
# paper/main.tex or book/main.tex in Overleaf → Menu → Main document.
# name
# manuscripts
